text:
alex: quick heads-up — the residency handoff we sketched in the rfc has a corner case when a tenant is under active traffic and a region is being drained. thinking about soft-handoff vs hard-evict and want opinions.

maya: agreed. main concern is PII-residency policies — we can’t move data out of eu without explicit consent, even if it's just cache copies.

sara: how often are we hitting that today? if most traffic is local the handoff is rare, but during rollout windows it spikes.

alex: spikes from deployments and scale tests are when this happens. i’m worried about split-brain where both regions think they own the shard after partial handoff.

luca: could we add a lightweight lease check with region-scoped leader election? e.g., write a lease key in the residency store and require renewals. if it lapses, other region can claim.

maya: lease helps but legal wants proof of deletion for eu tenants. we need an auditable state machine: TRANSFERRING -> TRANSFERRED -> DELETED.

sara: +1 on state machine but that implies durable transitions. any thought on where that state lives? residency-control plane? customer vault?

alex: plan: keep state in our control plane backed by per-tenant metadata (encrypted). actors: origin-region agent, target-region agent, control-plane coordinator. steps: 1) mark TRANSFERRING, 2) replicate KV prefix to target read-only, 3) switch routing to target, 4) confirm reads/writes, 5) purge origin copies if tenant policy allows -> mark DELETED.

luca: what about races if network partitions occur between step 3 and 4? need a fencing token so origin rejects writes once target is primary.

maya: fencing token + signed commit log works. ops-bot: runbook created: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/data-handoff (draft).

sara: for regulated tenants (eu-only) we should skip step 2 when policy forbids copies. instead do synchronous migration: pause writes, snapshot, import into target, update routing, resume — higher p99 but preserves residency.

alex: good call. so we’ll have two modes: copy-handoff (fast, eventual delete) and strict-move (pauses writes, auditable). we need automatic detection based on tenant policy.

luca: also add metrics: handoff_latency_ms, handoff_failure_count, stale_read_rate, lease_renew_failures. these will drive autosafety.

maya: canary idea: route 1% tenants through the new handoff path during rollout, with rollback flag if stale_read_rate > 0.1%.

sara: one more: make the handoff idempotent. include handoff_id in requests and idempotency table so retries don't flip states accidentally.

alex: agreed. follow-ups: (1) update residency rfc with state machine + fencing token, (2) add control-plane api endpoints: /handoff/start, /handoff/status, /handoff/confirm, /handoff/abort, (3) ops to author canary runbook.

maya: i'll draft the rfc snippet and add EU-specific flow.

luca: i'll prototype a lease/fence implementation in the runtime.

sara: ops-bot scheduled a design review: Thu 10am PT.

ops-bot: Reminder — design-review created: calendar.redwood/meeting/hand-off-1881234567 (Thu 10:00 PT).
